title: What the orchestration trials have shown
intro: See tested capabilities, their limits, and the work still ahead.

findings.label: Overview refreshed from local evidence
findings.title: Use current local commands with clear limits
findings.value: Find the observed executable paths and supported command grammar, with older baselines and unverified behavior clearly labelled.
findings.limit: Version/help and local path observations only. Runtime tool permissions, skill discovery, Agy’s current version and model behavior remain unqualified.
findings.details: The overview records observed Codex 0.166.0, Claude 2.1.316, Kiro 2.37.1 and Crush 0.93.1 plus portable PATH observations. Kiro’s manifest/reference remains at 2.37.0 with the gap explicit. Agy was not executed; 1.4.12 is last-recorded. Five help qualifications establish grammar only. Codex package/copy provenance and Crush global-rules discovery remain unknown, and historical containment failures are preserved. Independent reviews and current parent gates passed; 50 skills were deployed. No model session, permission change or renewed historical experiment occurred.
findings.diagramLabel: Use current local commands with clear limits

findings.label: Advisory takeover workflow shipped
findings.title: Keep unfinished work safe during a takeover
findings.value: Inspect inherited branches and checkouts, preserve needed source and evidence, and respect the app’s supported handoff.
findings.limit: Source review and synthetic local Git fixtures. No live checkout retirement, ignored/private evidence inventory, remote LFS recovery or branch disposition was qualified.
findings.details: An advisory procedure and read-only helper inventory local/cached refs and registered worktrees. Synthetic fixtures cover patch equivalence, unique and superseded source, uncertain merge history, target/candidate LFS rules and pointer/deletion cases. Source integration, evidence disposition and checkout retirement remain separate decisions. Both review axes accepted the final integrated source; focused and syntax checks passed, and 50 skills were deployed. The diagram describes the delivered workflow, not a performed retirement. Two historical checkouts disappeared during the session; original source refs remain, but their ignored-evidence recovery is unknown and no release is inferred.
findings.diagramLabel: Keep unfinished work safe during a takeover

findings.label: Review targets shipped
findings.title: Review work before making a commit
findings.value: Choose staged changes or tracked working files for review, with both reviewers inspecting the same captured version.
findings.limit: Actual staged documentation review and tracker isolation observed. Working-tree modes are documented; no claim of a live application review or simultaneous reviewer dispatch.
findings.details: The skill documents commit ranges, index-only, unstaged tracked and all tracked uncommitted modes, validates a nonempty target, separates untracked coverage, and checks reviewed bytes again before the verdict. Two independent contexts accepted an actual staged documentation patch; axes ran sequentially under capacity. A real tracker closure preserved that reviewed staged patch. Five push checks and syntax fixtures passed, and 50 skills were deployed. No production application behavior or simultaneous reviewer dispatch is claimed.
findings.diagramLabel: Review work before making a commit

findings.label: Installed behavior verified
findings.title: Keep staged work separate from ticket updates
findings.value: The installed tracker preserves staged implementation work when updating tickets. The historical sweep is fixed upstream.
findings.limit: Windows installed build and local-only synthetic fixtures. Network/hook latency and other argument forms remain unmeasured.
findings.details: Observed on installed tkt 0.4.0 (e755765): four ordinary local-only mutation fixtures committed only their ticket paths and kept the unrelated file staged. Independent reviewers checked the retained fixture indexes and commits. Query tags and tested single quoted comma arguments worked. No network/hook latency or other platform behavior is claimed. The workflow diagram represents the tested fixture behavior, not production application delivery.
findings.diagramLabel: Keep staged work separate from ticket updates

findings.label: Reassessment guidance shipped
findings.title: Tell a necessary repair from a stalled loop
findings.value: Review what changed in evidence and behavior before repeating preparation or adding more machinery.
findings.limit: Qualitative guidance, assessed on retained cases. No automatic retry cap or measured speed improvement is claimed.
findings.details: A necessary multi-step repair can grow while closing a real gap; preparation can stall without changing code. The orchestrator makes the first proportionality decision and retains the existing escalation boundary.
findings.diagramLabel: Tell a necessary repair from a stalled loop

findings.label: Proportionate intervention guidance shipped
findings.title: Choose a fix that matches the failure
findings.value: Separate a missing decision rule from a skipped instruction, a missing workflow step or a broken data contract.
findings.limit: Offline case assessment supports the guidance. An uncertain report remains uncertain; it does not justify another rule or validator.
findings.details: Contextual choices stay in the covering skill. Demonstrated data or syntax failures reuse the owning check; missing execution paths reuse an existing command. Existing guidance that was not followed is distinct from missing guidance.
findings.diagramLabel: Choose a fix that matches the failure

findings.label: Read-only coordination helper shipped
findings.title: Choose when to isolate work or reconcile updates
findings.value: Distinguish overlapping local work from updates pushed by another checkout.
findings.limit: Git state does not prove that an agent is live. Writer bindings are caller attestations; worktrees do not prevent remote push races.
findings.details: The read-only helper reports local changes, cached upstream advances and explicitly supplied writer evidence separately. It creates no lock, registry or background process and preserves unknown liveness.
findings.diagramLabel: Choose when to isolate work or reconcile updates

findings.label: Fact-based queue review shipped
findings.title: Keep unrelated tickets out of an execution queue
findings.value: Check exact workstream membership and report prerequisites or priorities that need attention.
findings.limit: Findings are advisory. Excluded work and external blockers remain visible; the helper does not change tickets or rewrite the queue.
findings.details: Full-board facts are filtered by exact tag rather than assuming a scoped query excludes untagged tickets. The review surfaces queue and backlog blockers, priority concerns and completed-looking criteria while preserving tracker authority.
findings.diagramLabel: Keep unrelated tickets out of an execution queue

findings.label: Receipt comparison shipped; broader checks open
findings.title: Reuse reviews that still match the page
findings.value: See which declared inputs changed before repeating captures and review.
findings.limit: Receipts cover declared inputs and captures. Custom-dashboard hooks and whole-board freshness checks remain unfinished.
findings.details: Read-only inspection preserves current accepted receipts for independently scoped views. Changed rendering inputs, captures or scope invalidate affected acceptance; shared inputs can invalidate several views. Pending or malformed evidence is never reusable.
findings.diagramLabel: Reuse reviews that still match the page

findings.label: Owned Claude follow-up confirmed
findings.title: Continue a task with the same Claude worker
findings.value: Send a follow-up and receive an answer that remembers the first exchange.
findings.diagramLabel: Keep the exchange in one worker
findings.limit: Confirmed for a bounded Windows text-worker session. Busy queues, reconnect and attachment to another chat remain unqualified.
findings.details: Two correlated turns completed with four core acknowledgments and two confirmed receipts. The observed owned process tree settled. Earlier failed and ambiguous cases remain preserved; this result does not establish served model identity or billing entitlement.

findings.label: Shared handoffs shipped
findings.title: Choose a tested worker handoff
findings.value: Keep a task with its worker, confirm replies and see when manual reporting is needed.
findings.diagramLabel: Choose a handoff route with clear limits
findings.limit: Bounded Windows exchanges are confirmed for desktop, Claude and Kiro workers. CLI delivery, unavailable permissions and held routes retain manual fallback.
findings.details: Shared routing, durable messages and receipt states distinguish a saved task from delivery and completion. Deterministic checks cover duplicate, restart and ambiguous outcomes. Native evidence is bounded to owned cases; it does not establish universal wakeup, foreign attachment, reconnect, exactly-once delivery or cross-platform parity.

findings.label: Owned desktop follow-up confirmed
findings.title: Continue a saved handoff with the same agent
findings.value: Send a saved question, then return to the same worker for a follow-up after it becomes idle.
findings.diagramLabel: Keep the exchange in one worker
findings.limit: The desktop exchange is confirmed. Exact busy-window timing and native CLI queue delivery remain unqualified; use manual reporting when a route is unavailable.
findings.details: The current stored-action format completed a same-target question and idle follow-up with a remembered nonce and validated core receipts. The first target was reported running; retained timing does not establish invocation inside its declared 30-second wait. Native identity/version are unreported and the witness is reconstructed. The separate fixed CLI queue adapter passes local refusal tests, while its native run stays held because the prelaunch integration gate is unresolved within current authorization.

findings.label: Owned Kiro handoff confirmed
findings.title: Continue a task with the same Kiro worker
findings.value: Send a follow-up to an owned worker and receive an answer that remembers the first exchange.
findings.diagramLabel: Two exchanges with one owned worker
findings.limit: Confirmed for one bounded V2 session. Busy queues, reconnect and V3 graceful shutdown remain unqualified.
findings.details: Both turns and their replies were acknowledged through the shared message core. The observed process tree settled. The original update stream reported a disconnect during owner stop; a local adapter correction passes fake-peer checks without rerunning the successful task. Served model identity and effective provider tool capacity remain unreported.

findings.label: Startup sequencing shipped
findings.title: Start Claude with the intended handoff
findings.value: The first saved handoff can start an owned worker without waiting for a readiness message that may require input.
findings.limit: The startup path and a bounded two-turn Windows exchange are confirmed. Broader session attachment and reconnect remain unqualified.
findings.details: The adapter allows one exact bound input while starting, keeps it busy across initialization and blocks another input until a correlated result. Local protocol checks pass. This startup change alone does not prove native delivery or completion. The later owned-session qualification completed both correlated turns and observed process settlement; earlier failures remain historical evidence.

findings.label: Handoff binding shipped
findings.title: Keep a handoff tied to the right worker
findings.value: Prepare owned-worker handoffs from the same saved message, keeping each input tied to its intended destination.
findings.diagramLabel: Prepare a handoff for its intended worker
findings.limit: Bounded owned Claude and Kiro exchanges are confirmed separately. Preparing an input alone does not prove delivery; held routes retain manual reporting.
findings.details: The shared intent now binds owned Claude and Kiro input to exact process generation, session and message identity. Independent review and 34 focused checks passed. Actual calls remain parent-owned; no new process, retry, grant or replacement conversation is created by preparation.

findings.label: Local lifecycle shipped
findings.title: See where a handoff stopped
findings.value: Separate a prepared handoff, an attempted send and a confirmed local receipt, so an uncertain result does not silently trigger another send.
findings.limit: Local receipt and send attestations do not prove native task completion. Expiry requires an explicit operator action.
findings.details: Deadline-bound intent events preserve unknown legacy state, prevent automatic resend and retain late receipts alongside earlier dead-letter history. Review caught false expiry when a spool receipt already existed; the corrected path and context compatibility pass the integrated 39-test suite. No scheduler or native invocation was added.

findings.label: Work context shipped
findings.title: Keep each handoff tied to the right work
findings.value: Carry the task, candidate and handoff reference together, so a reply stays connected to the work it belongs to.
findings.diagramLabel: Keep each handoff tied to the right work
findings.limit: These fields preserve supplied context. They do not verify the referenced file, commit or sender.
findings.details: Strict optional context participates in immutable message identity. Replies inherit it when omitted and reject a different ticket. Exact 40/64-character commit identity is required; old message hashes remain unchanged. Independently reviewed source and integrated 39-test suite passed. Native delivery remains separately qualified.

findings.label: Local process controls shipped
findings.title: Keep worker processes within clear limits
findings.value: Set a worker’s input, output and lifetime limits, then stop only the process that belongs to that work.
findings.diagramLabel: Keep worker processes within clear limits
findings.limit: Provider delivery still needs separate qualification. One platform-specific stop escalation case remains unverified on Windows.
findings.details: The shared internal process layer verifies executable identity, freezes startup inputs and preserves unrelated processes. Independent review reproduced a mutation bypass before acceptance; the corrected source passed12tests with0failures and1explicitWindowsSIGTERM escalation skip. Native provider protocols and completion are separate.

findings.label: Local route retirement shipped
findings.title: Close an old handoff route safely
findings.value: Close a past coordination route while preserving its message history, so it cannot accidentally receive new work.
findings.limit: This retires the local coordination route. It does not stop the native agent or prove native delivery.
findings.details: Exact target/version/generation retirement preserves other registrations and history. Strict input checks prevent malformed reply metadata or a response-kind bypass from poisoning persisted records. Parent and independent critic each passed23focusedtests. Real subprocess exits before/after atomic rename check bounded recovery and ambiguous-lock refusal; they do not prove power-loss safety. Native deadlines and broader messaging qualification remain in progress.

findings.label: Local checks and message records shipped
findings.title: Check a handoff before acting on it
findings.value: The coordinator can check the selected checkout, candidate, review evidence and prepared page. A local message record keeps queued, received and handled states separate.
findings.limit: These checks verify local records and prepared files. Human judgment and the actual remote publication result remain separate.
findings.details: Every current script candidate is classified and operator commands have specific task guidance. Dispatch checks passed eight fixtures and an actual completed-worker checkout. Publication checks passed ten fixtures and the actual known link-transformed Site payload. The spool passed eleven identity/lifecycle/restart/permission fixtures. The outcome-trace auditor rejects inconsistent scope, review, capacity, stop and delivery claims; those event claims remain attestations. Independent critics reviewed exact final candidates. No model default or global harness setting changed.

findings.label: Outcome guidance and local safeguards shipped
findings.title: Give the coordinator an outcome and a clear finish line
findings.value: You can start a session around what needs to be delivered. The guidance keeps work moving through review and integration, with explicit reasons to pause or stop.
findings.limit: Background continuation and delivery across other harnesses remain unqualified.
findings.details: The outcome contract names scope, authority, resources, proof and stop conditions. User and authorized-agent invocation policies agree. Reviewer capacity, separate task/cleanup/delivery observations and current monitor state are explicit. Independent critic accepted candidate bdf2f182; parent integrated and passed the selected checks, then deployed with Agy excluded. No native model or goal run was used to qualify this slice. The effort queue also displays its existing shared-messaging dependency, whose ticket retains tooling-stream ownership.

findings.label: Workaround documented; native shutdown unresolved
findings.title: Keep completed work when a worker reports a shutdown error
findings.value: Kiro workers can complete a task and then report a shutdown error. The workflow now checks the work and cleanup separately, so that error alone does not trigger duplicate work.
findings.limit: Graceful unattended shutdown remains unqualified. Deeper repair research is deferred until higher-priority work is finished.
findings.details: The user accepted the known limitation and closed the diagnosis. Only the exact observed five-second EOF error receives the teardown classification; other failures still need diagnosis. Native completion plus independent artifact and critic checks are required for task acceptance. Bounded descendant observation must establish cleanup separately; a live or unobserved process remains unresolved. Session close is not a proven engine shutdown and session deletion is not a remedy. No new native probe ran. Existing raw evidence and four model-bearing sessions remain retained for the low-priority follow-up.

findings.label: Protocol documented; no new client trial
findings.title: Keep supervision around a standard agent connection
findings.value: ACP can carry requests, progress and approval questions. A supervisor still needs to choose work, isolate it and decide what to accept.
findings.diagramLabel: Documented boundary, compared with earlier probes
findings.limit: The SDK was not installed or measured. Runtime findings come from earlier named driver probes; no portable-client or cost advantage was demonstrated.
findings.details: The source audit distinguishes the SDK package version from stable ACP v1 and experimental v2 schemas, plus the separate MCP tool-server boundary and Kiro extensions. Earlier Windows probes observed Kiro request, follow-up, approval visibility, cancellation and load behavior. The Kiro EOF shutdown issue remains specific to that implementation. Mixed-backend setup and generic client ownership are separate questions. No additional actionable spike is recommended without a concrete client need; no new native probe, installation or account setting change occurred.

findings.label: Effort trial incomplete; defaults retained
findings.title: Keep effort defaults until quality can be compared
findings.value: The trial did not establish a better effort level. Incomplete runs and unusable review evidence prevent a fair quality comparison.
findings.limit: Actual effort was not reported, and most review receipts were invalid. The single usable score cannot establish an effort-level advantage.
findings.details: Thirteen native calls produced eleven complete responses and two timeouts; one additional cell failed setup before a model call. One response had a valid blind pass and ten are unscorable because their review receipts failed validation. These are evidence gaps, not model-quality failures. The passing requested Codex max result lacked served model and actual effort. Kiro and Google cohorts remained held. Unknown costs and timeout usage remain unknown. Twenty authorized empty working directories were recycled and their source paths verified absent; destination identifiers were not recorded. No defaults changed.

findings.label: Rewrites passed; triage and classification need care
findings.title: Keep human checks beside routine text work
findings.value: All six profiles handled the small rewrite. Triage and changelog classification exposed mistakes, so none qualified to replace the current defaults across these tasks.
findings.limit: One observation per task and profile does not establish reliability. Missing served identities and costs also limit the comparison.
findings.details: Eighteen native responses received blind reviews: seven passed and eleven failed. No profile passed all three tasks. Claude reported Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5.5; Codex and Kiro omitted served identity and dollar cost. Google remained held without a call. Review provenance is parent-transcribed rather than a platform export; one failed review-file write has no initial semantic bytes for comparison. Six exact Kiro sessions were removed while all 7,600 non-target session/source pairs were preserved. No default or global setting changed.

findings.label: Correct code observed; full workflow proof incomplete
findings.title: Keep default coding workers while the full job is unproven
findings.value: Cheaper workers produced correct code in several tasks. Missing test proof and mistakes on unclear requests kept them from qualifying as replacements for the current defaults.
findings.limit: One run per task and profile does not establish reliability. Harness and policy interruptions prevented several fair comparisons.
findings.details: The trial attempted 38 of 48 planned cells. Claude's implementation artifacts passed, but native output did not prove successful agent test execution. Kiro's ordinary tasks passed; the cheaper requested profile guessed a missing style in an ambiguity case. Codex's incomplete launch path failed before a fair comparison. Agy execution remains held after a security stop. Served identity and costs were missing for some providers; Claude costs are list estimates, not billing. No default or global permission changed.

findings.label: Planted defects found; strict review output incomplete
findings.title: Check review findings before using them as a gate
findings.value: Reviewers found the planted problems in these small cases. Unsupported extra claims and output-format failures leave cheaper automated review unqualified.
findings.limit: Four small cases do not establish production review quality. One requested cheaper alias served a different model.
findings.details: Fourteen of 23 attempts met the required JSON format. Secondary blind scoring found the seeded defect and changed-line citation in all 22 nonempty responses, with nine unsupported claims and five duplicate findings. One startup failure produced no response. No cheaper profile covered all four strict-format cases. Claude's requested haiku alias served Sonnet 5.5; Codex and Kiro did not report actual identity. The earlier unintended help turn had unknown usage, so total budget compliance remains unverified. Google was held without a call.

findings.label: Accuracy tested; model choice unchanged
findings.title: Keep source checks beside delegated research
findings.value: Most scored answers met the small research tasks. Missing citations, an oversized summary and gaps in review evidence kept the trial from qualifying a cheaper model.
findings.limit: Five of 18 results were unscorable. Some model identities were absent; retained reviewer traces were producer-transcribed rather than platform exports.
findings.details: Thirteen valid review receipts yielded eleven passes and two failures. A Haiku summary exceeded the word cap and added an unsupported claim; a requested cheap Kiro answer omitted the required citation heading. Three review receipts failed validation, and two earlier passing receipts lacked retained dispatch evidence; neither gap counts as a model failure or verified pass. The requested cheap Codex profile passed all three tasks, but its actual model was unreported. Keep defaults. Exact native sessions and empty work directories were cleaned; private evidence remains retained for the remaining trials.

findings.label: Shared tasks demonstrated; tier trials underway
findings.title: Compare workers on the same tasks
findings.value: Two small implementation tasks ran through two assistants with separate workspaces and independent checks. The same approach now supports the next model trials.
findings.limit: These were task demonstrations, not a model ranking. Other task types still need their own fixtures; the host setup did not provide an isolation boundary.
findings.details: The selected Windows-native runner preserves requested versus observed model identity, native usage and independent grading. Its hardened grader catches staged, untracked and committed changes outside allowed paths and rejects unexpected commits. Claude costs are native list estimates; Codex dollar cost and observed identity were absent. Harbor's local setup was blocked before execution, while remote modes remain untested. Implementation and review trials are now dispatched separately; measured model runs are serialized.

findings.label: Candidates documented; live steering unverified
findings.title: Compare native views before relying on them
findings.value: Five interfaces were compared for worker status, approvals, questions and usage. The comparison separates documented features from what could actually be observed here.
findings.limit: No GUI was verified to display or steer the retained headless workers. Launch or capture failed, or automation was unavailable by policy.
findings.details: Claude Agent View is CLI/TUI and separate from the Desktop sidebar. Codex app-list state labels were unspecified in reviewed docs; Kiro Agent Focus and Crew chat document replies for their own sessions. Antigravity app subagent views differ from CLI approval controls. Crew usage documentation was older than the local install. Keep native worker results and the controller ledger authoritative until exact session mapping and an actual interaction are proven.

findings.label: Recipe launch and retry observed
findings.title: Follow a multi-step run and guide it from a monitor
findings.value: A recipe started, showed step results, accepted guidance and retried a failed step. The run reached its final step but did not complete.
findings.limit: A safe pause boundary and a complete review-and-merge loop remain unverified. The recipe does not create separate worktrees or guarantee independent review.
findings.details: Kiro V3 ran a four-step local recipe under private settings. A pause request appeared, but the capture did not establish a completed safe-boundary pause. Read-only fixture tools appeared during ambiguous approval interaction; no policy-bypass conclusion is supported. Inherited global-hook isolation was not established, and no isolated worker commit or landing was observed.

findings.label: One read-only project check confirmed
findings.title: Use the complete installation to run a project check
findings.value: A read-only project check ran from the complete installed package. The standalone copy had failed before the check could start.
findings.limit: This verified one harmless check, not writes or approval behavior. The tested internal package path may change after an update; no durable installation repair was made.
findings.details: Codex's two stable executable copies had identical version and bytes. The PATH-selected copy lacked its sibling code-mode host; the installed Windows platform package contained the signed companion and executed the exact fixture Git status command. No binary copy, install or global configuration edit was used. Earlier message-board and wake probes remain historically unverified.

findings.label: One message and idle notice confirmed
findings.title: Send a background worker a message and hear when its turn ends
findings.value: A background worker received a message, replied, and sent a separate idle notice. This gives the controller a signal to inspect the result.
findings.limit: Idle does not mean the work is accepted. The test project's trust check blocked background dispatch and automatic worktree creation; those paths remain unverified.
findings.details: Claude Code's native message call and receiver transcript confirmed one same-machine exchange. The preliminary marker session belonged to the isolated worker checkout and was stopped and removed after review. Safe branch pushes and the documented idle reaper were not tested. No persistent project trust was accepted; only after-run settings hashes were captured.

findings.label: Typed jobs confirmed; model selection unresolved
findings.title: Collect structured results from jobs in separate work areas
findings.value: Two jobs ran in separate worktrees and returned checked results. One worker asked for a missing name, then continued in the same conversation when given an answer.
findings.limit: The answer and admission choices were scripted. Review and merging were checked outside the workflow; per-role model selection remains unverified.
findings.details: Native agy parallel and sequential controls completed. An invalid result was rejected before correction. The two ticket commits changed only their assigned files; independent controller inspection, merges and combined tests passed. Earlier attempts stopped on narrow permission denials. No global settings changed. The routing qualification found documented request controls but no verified child-scoped served-model identity. Opaque labels and requested tiers cannot establish cost or capability guarantees.

findings.label: Matching confirmed; approval overlap unresolved
findings.title: Give a worker access to a smaller set of actions
findings.value: Selected Git, test and ticket-reading commands ran with narrow grants. A folder grant allowed a nested file while rejecting a nearby sibling path.
findings.limit: Fresh controls reproduced the regex approval mismatch; its cause remains unknown. Do not rely on that override. These checks do not establish whole-machine confinement.
findings.details: The headless Windows agy trial checked native tool results and actual file bytes. Exact literal grants also worked. TEMP writes have a default grant, so the path test moved outside TEMP and the workspace. A fresh matching Deny rule rejected the tested command; use a separately validated blocking rule where blocking is intended. No effective permission list was obtained and no global settings changed. The sanitized upstream issue brief remains local, not submitted.

findings.label: Recovery confirmed; planning needs oversight
findings.title: Resume a worker after a gateway restart
findings.value: A standing teammate reconnected with the same worker after a graceful restart. The worker remembered its earlier reply, and its fresh report woke the teammate.
findings.limit: The teammate then invented the next task. Keep requirements and acceptance checks outside that loop. Crashes during active work were not tested.
findings.details: The private Kiro Crew trial restored the persisted parent link and reused the worker's native session. The old completed report did not replay in the startup observation window. After a controller corrected the invented task, the same worker implemented the actual multiply fixture and its tests passed. No independent Mate review or merge was established, so superiority over the built-in conductor remains unproven.

findings.label: Confirmed in fixtures
findings.title: Split work into small jobs, then review before merging
findings.value: Independent jobs ran in separate work areas. A review step checked the result before accepted changes were brought together.
findings.limit: These were small test projects. A worker's claim of success was never enough on its own.
findings.details: The authored skill dry runs exercised Claude Code and Kiro CLI. Earlier baseline spikes covered Codex, Kiro Crew and Antigravity with different limitations. Admission held overlapping and dependent jobs; the later dry runs held the risky deletion rather than dispatching it.

findings.label: Confirmed in tested sessions
findings.title: A worker can ask a question and continue with the answer
findings.value: The tested sessions remembered their context when the controller supplied a missing name. Some continued in one process; others resumed in a fresh process.
findings.limit: This confirms the captured exchanges, not recovery from every kind of interruption.
findings.details: Claude and Antigravity carried paired-stream follow-ups. Codex exec/resume and Kiro chat/resume kept the same session identity. Kiro ACP loaded a saved conversation and produced a fresh answer after replayed history; replay was not counted as a new answer.

findings.label: One safety case confirmed
findings.title: The tested deletion can stop for a human decision
findings.value: A restrictive policy blocked deletion of the project README, and the worker reported that it needed a human ruling.
findings.limit: Ordinary allowed commands still asked for approval. Broad containment and unattended operation are not established.
findings.details: This was an owner-scoped KAS policy with YOLO off. It protects one tested command form, not all deletion routes or arbitrary process access. Earlier broad-trust runs did delete and merge the README, so permission setup materially changes the outcome.

findings.label: Failure signals observed
findings.title: Check the work result before calling a run successful
findings.value: A run can finish cleanly while a command was denied. Native tool results exposed that difference in the comparison.
findings.limit: There is no single exit code or status word that proves accepted work across all of these drivers.
findings.details: Antigravity returned SUCCESS and exit 0 with an empty response after automatic command denial. Codex completed a text turn while tool execution was blocked by a missing companion host. Kiro's live ACP request/cancel/load worked, but EOF shutdown still exited 1. The follow-up tickets separate these infrastructure limits from transport results.

sources.label: Codex dispatch controls and setup limit

findings.label: Callback route tested; real delivery untested
findings.title: Choose the sign-in owner explicitly
findings.value: The bundled engine asked a test host for credentials and returned the expected error when none were supplied. A documented setting selects this route.
findings.limit: Real Crew credential-vault delivery was not tested. This exercised the bundled engine's callback path, not a full signed-in Crew session.
findings.details: Crew 0.11.1's Windows relay host-auth builder still omitted the owner flag. Its documented agent.kas_bundle=true route selects bundled KAS with explicit callback authentication. The private KAS 0.66.33 probe received eight credential requests and failed with the expected credential-unavailable error. CLI-owned success is historical evidence from the exact matching CLI 2.37.1 binary. No tokens, account changes or installed product patches were used.

findings.label: Optional integration confirmed
findings.title: Keep the ticket and worker state aligned
findings.value: The optional integration mirrored active, waiting, review and completed states into the worker's native bookkeeping.
findings.limit: The ticket tracker stays authoritative. Missing optional tools are skipped; this does not add a requirement to every harness.
findings.details: The guarded Kiro Crew integration was independently checked against native tags and ledger fields. It provides visibility metadata, not evidence that the implementation or a GUI review passed.

possibilities.title: Watch and answer through a familiar interface
possibilities.value: Compare which interfaces show worker state and let a person answer questions or approvals.

possibilities.title: Spend less without losing the quality bar
possibilities.value: Haiku and Luna were included in the completed model comparisons. The evidence still supports keeping defaults; the separate paid-fast-mode question was retired after your clarification.
